I'm a mediocre piano player. It takes effort for me to read the notes and play them for the first time. I have to practice each section individually on each hand, then combine it. After practicing a piece for a while, I can play it from memory effortlessly. If I don't play a piece for a while, I might have to glance at the notes to get going again, but the muscle memory comes back quick.

I am a world class piano-playing singer and do both simultaneously. For me, the early lessons of piano (age 3) paved the way for it to be second nature as 30+ years of constant playing have developed. Can you walk and chew gum at the same time? I find singing and playing piano the same type of thing -- playing piano is like walking and singing is like chewing gum. Though the technique of singing is more taxing on the body with proper breath support etc needed. The combination of the two is a constant back and forth of technique and ease.
